sourceReinspections.observations: The design-process bullet explicitly says iterative; red underlining emphasizes number of joints, arrangement and actuation/sensing schemes continuously refined.
The bold aliases are jointed, elbow and anthropomorphic. The two drawings show side and top views with shoulder/elbow angles and workspace sectors.

The first bullet visibly reads SCARA stands for Selectively Compliant Assembly Robot Arm. Assembly, not Articulated, is underlined on the supplied source. The separate three-revolute/fourth-prismatic wording and pictured d3 mismatch remain a known source qualification.
The source displays det(J)=0 for the square case and w=sqrt(det(JJ transpose)); rank reasoning is task-relative and rectangular matrices require the Gram expression.
The source forward map uses the relative elbow angle theta1+theta2, lengths5 and4 and both joint intervals[-pi,pi].
The source gives continuous radial limits1 and9 and R=sqrt(x squared+y squared); its all-points language must not be transferred to a finite sample.

Actual code uses two inclusive linspace arrays of200 points, doubly nested loops and paired x/y appends. The ordinary quoted title visibly wraps over two lines; literal parsing and intended repaired execution must be distinguished.

priorAuthorExposure: I independently reviewed all original83 items. Sixteen repairs are therefore not first-exposure blind reviews. Q084 andQ085 are new, and neither author key/solution has been opened. The current-version responses are frozen before opening the current keyed batch.

independentAnswers.reasoning: A mechanical loop imposes closure constraints, so joint freedoms need not be independent. Summing all individual freedoms or counting only actuators misses those constraints and passive freedoms.

Task redundancy means more independent configuration freedoms than the task requires. Too few freedoms can prevent a general task; neither an open chain nor a controller definition reverses that inequality.

Rapid-motion load capacity depends on the complete structure, transmission and actuator capability together with configuration leverage and inertial/velocity-dependent loading. Static weight alone or peak speed alone is insufficient.

The cited design simplifications are twists of 0 or plus/minus 90 degrees where appropriate, intersecting wrist axes, and many zero lengths or offsets. Arbitrary skew axes and increased length alone do not guarantee easy inverse kinematics.
The ideal planar minimum radius is the absolute difference of the positive lengths. Equal lengths allow fully folded reach to zero; the other radii are now distinct alternatives.

A task Jacobian rank drop removes one or more independent instantaneous task-velocity directions. It need not remove configuration coordinates, every velocity direction or every finite reachable nearby point.

For a real m-by-n Jacobian with m<=n, zero determinant of the row Gram matrix means dependent rows. Dependent columns alone are normal for a redundant full-row-rank Jacobian and do not force zero row-Gram determinant.
Ordinary J inverse and inverse transpose require a square nonsingular J; all matrices must refer to compatible coordinates and configuration. The mass matrix cannot cancel a missing ordinary inverse.
Squaring and adding cancels first-angle dependence and yields l1 squared plus l2 squared plus 2*l1*l2*cos(theta2). With 5 and 4, this is 41+40cos(theta2).
The four named target radii are: (1,0)->1; (0,9)->9; (3,4)->5; (0.6,0.6)->sqrt(0.72)<1. Only the last is outside the allowed closed annulus 1<=r<=9.
An unescaped physical newline inside an ordinary short single-quoted string causes a SyntaxError at parsing. Call parentheses do not permit that literal form.
Every combination of 200 first angles and 200 second angles is visited, yielding 40000 appended x entries and 40000 corresponding y entries, not necessarily 40000 distinct Cartesian positions.

An inclusive 200-point interval has 199 gaps. The nearest theta2 values to zero are plus/minus pi/199, so the maximum sampled radius is sqrt(41+40cos(pi/199)), strictly below 9. Endpoint inclusion gives theta2=plus/minus pi, not zero.
The Cartesian-product grid grows from 200 squared to 400 squared, so FK evaluations and stored coordinate pairs both quadruple from 40000 to 160000.

Axial tool symmetry can remove an axial-roll requirement but does not grant arbitrary tool-axis directions at each position. The pictured two rotations plus radial slide form a three-motion positioner, not a general six-coordinate pose mechanism.

Differentiating with rows(x,y) and columns(theta1,theta2) gives [[-l1*s1-l2*s12,-l2*s12],[l1*c1+l2*c12,l2*c12]]. Its determinant is l1*l2*(s12*c1-s1*c12)=l1*l2*sin(theta2), zero at 0 and plus/minus pi. Omitting the distal contribution to column 1 can retain this determinant but yields the wrong complete Jacobian.

Actual page 548 explicitly calls design iterative and continuously refines joint count/arrangement with actuation and sensing. Passing reachability alone does not establish moving-inertia, cycle-time or precision performance, so the coupled choices must be reevaluated.

Actual page 558 lists articulated aliases jointed, elbow and anthropomorphic. Actual page 560 visibly expands SCARA as Selectively Compliant Assembly Robot Arm, not Articulated Robot Arm. Therefore the exact source-specific match is option o4. No author key or solution for this new gap was consulted.
